### Text/UI-aware routing: detect text/line-art content and route it to a competing encoding profile

`active` · `@jpegxl-rs.work.text-aware-routing/4` · part of `@jpegxl-rs.track.perceptual-quality-controller/1` · **at risk**

Close the text/UI density gap. Stage 1 (DONE): corpus gap measured - geomean 1.15x ZenJXL / 1.39x cjxl, max 4.7x. Stage 2 (DONE): shadow content classifier (content_class.rs, 4e10611). Stage 3 (SHIPPED opt-in, 94e8dc4): --text-routing / Encoder::with_text_routing - deterministic median-cut colour reduction, canonical scoring through the evaluator's retained reference, lossless Modular candidates, first floor-holding rung wins, replaces VarDCT only when smaller or the search missed. Corpus A/B: -21% bytes, 69/121 smaller, 0 grew, 0 floor violations. Stage 4 B4 (DONE, cf94f5f): wall bounded - trace attribution showed candidate encode = 96% of competition wall, so the ladder is score-first over one shared colour histogram with exactly one encode per frame at Modular effort 2 (palette plan wins at every effort: candidate bytes identical e2/e3/e5 across the corpus). Routed overhead median 0.77->0.58 s, p90 2.27->1.33 s, max 7.20->2.30 s; VarDCT-wins premium median 0.75 s. REMAINING: the default-on decision is the operator's - it needs the standing Contract-B A/B screen when proposed. Beyond this work: the residual worst-case gap (~2-3x on a few screens vs ZenJXL) needs a lossy-smooth text representation (patches/mode switching) - a separate future feature; a CIELAB Wu-style quantizer (operator's own WuElast reference is portable) is a possible palette-quality upgrade if k-rung floor failures ever matter.

## Unparented

### Assert jpxl-perceptual's default feature set stays codec-free, as tests/boundary.rs already does for the other two edges

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.work.assert-perceptual-default-is-codec-free-2026-09-08/1`

jpxl-perceptual's independence from the JPXL codec crates is real and
deliberate but is not asserted anywhere. crates/jpxl-perceptual/Cargo.toml sets
`default = []` and marks every codec dependency optional: jpxl-core enters only
through the `evaluator` feature (with jpxl-encode-policy and jpxl-plan-render),
jpxl-encode only through `encode-executor`, and the rust-av ssimulacra2 crate
only through the test-only `parity-oracle`. The manifest comment says so and
cites jpegxl-rs.policy.perceptual-metric-clean-room. That shape is what lets
jp2lam, in Lege-ecosystem/lege-codecs, path-depend on jpxl-perceptual with
default-features = false and share the `ssimulacra2-jpxl-1` metric identity
without taking the encoder.

It surfaced 2026-09-08 as a false alarm that cost someone a diagnosis: a
`cargo check --workspace` in Lege-ecosystem rewrote its Cargo.lock and dropped
jpxl-bitstream and jpxl-core, which looks like a broken dependency until you
read jpxl-perceptual's feature table and see it is the intended default
resolution. A one-line assertion would have answered that in the time it takes
to run a test.

crates/jpxl-encode-policy/tests/boundary.rs already does exactly this job for
the other two edges -- `jpxl_encode_does_not_depend_on_policy` and
`policy_does_not_depend_on_the_decoder`, both reading the manifest text through
a shared `dependencies_section` helper. The gap is that nothing stops someone
adding `evaluator` to jpxl-perceptual's `default` list, which would silently put
jpxl-core, jpxl-encode-policy and jpxl-plan-render into every downstream build
including jp2lam's.

The work: a third test in the same file (or in jpxl-perceptual's own tests,
which is arguably the better home since it is that crate's invariant) asserting
that jpxl-perceptual's `[features] default` is empty and that every JPXL
dependency in its manifest carries `optional = true`. Ten or so lines, same
manifest-text technique as the two that exist. The decision the next session
should make is only where it lives, and whether it should also pin that
`parity-oracle` never appears in a default or non-test feature, since that is
the arm that would pull a third-party metric into a production build.

### Decide whether the ledger's normative layer should be active rather than proposed

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.work.normative-layer-still-proposed-2026-09-08/1`

Six constraints, seventeen decisions and thirteen policies sit at state
`proposed` while plainly governing the code today -- among them
constraint.forbid-unsafe-by-default, constraint.no-panic-checked-arith,
constraint.no-libjxl-runtime-dep, policy.clean-room-boundary,
decision.optimization-determinism-contract and decision.perceptual-quality-contract.
AKR treats `proposed` and `active` as both valid initial states for a normative
record, so nothing is broken; but a reader cannot tell a rule that is merely
drafted from one the crate graph and CI enforce, and that is the whole point of
the distinction.

This pass activated exactly two, where the evidence link was unambiguous and the
cross-project licence boundary made it matter:
decision.mit-only-licensing (all twelve crates declare MIT via license.workspace,
LICENSE and JPXL/LICENSE-MIT agree, and a full dependency-graph scan found no
copyleft -- evidence.mit-only-licensing-audit-2026-08-25) and
policy.perceptual-metric-clean-room (jpxl-decode appears only in the policy
crate's [dev-dependencies], enforced by tests/boundary.rs).

The rest were left alone deliberately, because activating a decision trips
AKR-R031 unless it cites a requirement, policy, constraint or evidence, and
guessing those citations one by one is how a ledger acquires fiction. Someone who
knows the project should sweep them: for each, either cite what motivated it and
move it to `active`, or leave it `proposed` on purpose and say why. A third
outcome is also legitimate -- if the project's convention is that `proposed`
simply means "recorded", write that down as a ledger-convention decision (there
is already a decision.ledger-conventions to revise) and stop treating the gap as
a defect.

### Retire or re-measure the 52-record stale measurement backlog in the review queue

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.work.stale-measurement-backlog-2026-09-08/1`

After the 2026-09-08 ledger pass the review queue holds 52 stale records (down
from 70) and 36 at risk. What is left is not noise: with one exception every
remaining record watches a specific file that really did change, and the
concentration says where -- 8 on jpxl-encode-policy/src/lib.rs, 6 on quality.rs,
5 on rate.rs, 4 on quantize.rs. These are dated measurements of the encoder's
hot policy path taken between 2026-08-10 and 2026-09-03, and the path has been
rewritten under them repeatedly (Opt-F..Opt-P, the fused probe-render work, the
one-shot controller, the case-table predictor).

The decision this needs, and that a bookkeeping pass cannot make, is a policy one:
what should happen to an empirical record whose subject file has moved on. Three
candidate answers, and the project should pick one and apply it uniformly.
(a) Nothing: a measurement is a fact about a commit, it is true forever, and the
right fix is to strip `watches` from measurement observations so they stop
entering the queue at all -- which is what this pass did for the 18 spec-reading
observations imported at f35cabcf, whose claims were about the ISO text and could
never go stale from a code change. (b) Re-measure: run the benchmark again at
HEAD and `akr revise` with fresh numbers. This is a dedicated measurement session
with a quiet host, not a cleanup task; note
jpegxl-rs.observation.measuring-host-cannot-resolve-small-effects-2026-08-31.
(c) Retire: mark them superseded by whatever later measurement replaced them,
where one exists.

(a) is almost certainly right for most of them and is nearly free. (b) is right
only where a live decision still rests on the number.

Three records were triaged as genuinely unknown and should be settled first,
because a wrong answer in these three could mislead rather than merely age:
- observation.pqc-one-shot-gate-fails-on-corpus-coverage-2026-08-24 -- 08859157
  was explicitly camera-coverage work, the exact gap this record names. Settle by
  diffing the current class counts in quality_predictor_cases.rs (now a 1203-case
  table) against the classes the record calls under-represented.
- observation.balanced-zero-prediction-reserve-negative -- 23635f68 rewrote the
  reserve and prediction logic broadly. Settle by reading the current
  reserve-coupled band code in rate.rs against the measured regression claimed.
- observation.ssimulacra2-f32-recursion-ripple-2026-08-22 -- 2425c0b2 touched
  blur.rs directly (103 lines). Settle by checking whether the Gaussian recursion
  still runs in f64. Carries review 2026-11-30, so already deprioritised.

Two over-broad globs also survive and should be narrowed to the files each record
actually cites: "JPXL/tools/**" on measuring-host-cannot-resolve-small-effects and
three-way-encoder-comparison (a corpus-generation script edit re-stales both), and
"JPXL/crates/jpxl-perceptual/src/**" on pqc-wall-attribution-post-s2 and
wall-anchors-after-2026-08-31-cuts (a brand-new unrelated file, bands.rs, re-staled
both). All 36 at-risk records inherit from this set and clear when it does.
